name: RC-B10-0173/2024 – After recital H – Am 12
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the Council’s recommendation on smoke- and aerosol-free environments
part_text: Ha. whereas in Europe, the most common method of using cannabis still appears to be smoking it mixed with tobacco1a; whereas this brings additional health risks, while the associated nicotine dependence may also make treatment more difficult; whereas addressing the specific harm associated with smoking cannabis, especially in combination with tobacco, is an important but neglected topic; whereas smoking cannabis has physical and mental health consequences, some of which are irreversible; whereas the tobacco-free generation should also be understood as cannabis-free; whereas second-hand cannabis smoke contains many of the same toxic and cancer-causing chemicals found in tobacco smoke, some in higher amounts; whereas second-hand cannabis smoke also contains tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the compound responsible for most of cannabis’s psychoactive effects; whereas cannabis remains by far the most commonly consumed illicit drug in Europe1b; whereas cannabis use can cause or exacerbate a range of physical and mental health problems, including chronic respiratory symptoms, cannabis dependence and psychotic symptoms; whereas in addition, studies have found that regular cannabis use can be associated with poorer educational achievement and an increased risk of involvement with the criminal justice system; whereas an approach whereby cannabis is tolerated or regulated gives rise to the concern that cannabis is still necessarily supplied from the illegal market, and criminal groups therefore benefit from this trade; \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ 1a European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction, ‘Cannabis: health and social responses’, 2023, [https://www.euda.europa.eu/publications/mini-guides/cannabis-health-and-social-responses\_en](https://www.euda.europa.eu/publications/mini-guides/cannabis-health-and-social-responses_en). 1b European Monitoring Centre for Drugs and Drug Addiction, ‘Cannabis – the current situation in Europe (European Drug Report 2024)’, [https://www.euda.europa.eu/publications/european-drug-report/2024/cannabis\_en#level-1-section1](https://www.euda.europa.eu/publications/european-drug-report/2024/cannabis_en#level-1-section1).
